about: The response envelopes POST /verify and POST /verify/batch answer with, as data.
Consumed by tests/integration/src/conformance/wireContract.mts and by
packages/server/src/__tests__/verifyInputValidation.test.mts, which reads
`error.documentedExample` rather than keeping a second copy of it. An enforcement
layer implementing against this endpoint (o3co/protobuf.interceptors) can read the
same file: it is JSON at a stable path, not a TypeScript literal.
Key lists are EXHAUSTIVE. A response carrying a key not named here is drift, and
the suite fails on the extra key as readily as on a missing one — an enforcement
layer that switched on a field this contract never promised is exactly the coupling
#125 exists to prevent.
Three vocabulary notes (#182). `attribute_conflict` is a deny code and arrives
with `status.deny`, wearing the decision envelope like `collector_timeout`.
`internal_error` is the terminal envelope — the one 5xx in this table, still
shaped like `error` so a client parsing only decision JSON reads it as a deny.
`caller_unauthenticated` is the optional `http.callerAuth` gate's refusal (#108):
the gate sits IN FRONT of this surface and answers before the body is parsed, so
it appears in `codes`/`status` but never as a request case — where a deployment
sets the gate, every refusal below is reachable only through it.
`requestId` (#200) is the one response HEADER this table pins. An `x-request-id`
the request carried is echoed on every response the two endpoints write when it is
at most `maxLength` characters matching `pattern`; any other value is treated as if
none was sent, and none is ever minted. The gate above answers before this surface
and does not echo it.
`evaluation` (#244) is the one OPTIONAL key of a rule outcome: what a policy-backed
rule reported about the evaluation behind that answer — whether its evaluator ran,
and which policy revision it concerned. A deployment sends it only under
`verify.evaluationInResponse = "include"`, and only for a rule that reported one, so
ABSENCE IS THE MIXED-VERSION CASE AND MEANS UNKNOWN: an older verifier, a deployment
that did not opt in and a rule with no policy source all answer without it, and a
client that requires a revision must treat all three alike. `revision` is a claim
about what was EVALUATED: a string only when the evaluator vouched for it, `null` when
it ran and what it evaluated cannot be established (a remote engine that does not
say). What the verifier LOADED is then carried apart as `loadedRevision`, which is not
proof of what ran. `not_invoked` carries no revision key of either kind. A deny made
without a policy evaluation (`collector_timeout`, `rule_timeout`, `attribute_conflict`,
`no_applicable_rule`) has no groups and therefore no evaluation: no policy decided it.
The key sets under `evaluation` below are what THIS version sends, and the suite holds
a DEPLOYMENT to them exactly. A CLIENT reads the other way: it MUST IGNORE any key inside
`evaluation` that it does not know, and a client that rejects an unknown key breaks on
the verifier's next minor.
`determiningPolicies` (#199) names the policies that determined a COMPLETED answer — for
an allow the permits that applied, for a deny the forbids that did — and is an empty list
when no policy applied. It is a set of policy ids, named as the rule's producer documents
them, at most `determiningPolicies.maxItems` of them; whatever the evaluator named beyond
that, or in a shape it could not carry, is counted in `determiningPoliciesOmitted`, present
only beside the list and only when it is not zero. Beside `revision: null` the ids are as
unconfirmed as the revision. A `failed` or `not_invoked` evaluation carries neither key:
no policy decided that answer. ABSENT means the rule did not say.

determiningPolicies.about: A set of distinct policy ids. Each is well-formed UTF-16 (no lone surrogate), 1 to idMaxLength UTF-16 code units long, and holds no code point in idForbiddenRanges (inclusive, hex): the controls, and the characters that break or reorder a displayed line or hide in it. `determiningPoliciesOmitted` is an integer of at least `omitted.minimum`, present only beside the list.

revision.about: scheme:encoded, the OCI digest grammar — `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` for a content digest. Never a path, a label with spaces or policy text; `revision` may instead be null, `loadedRevision` may not.

requestId.echoedOn: every response POST /verify and POST /verify/batch write — allow, deny, batch, every refusal in this table and internal_error — when the request carried an id within maxLength matching pattern
requestId.otherwise: no x-request-id response header: an id outside the shape is treated as absent, and none is minted when the request carried none
